title: Claude Haiku 5.5
summary: Anthropic released claude-haiku-5-5, billed as its cheapest, fastest, and most capable small model, at about 75% lower cost than Haiku 4.5 on average and as the first Haiku-class model with adjustable effort. Sonnet 5.5's cache-read price was halved, Max and Team get monthly API credits, and OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset) rose from 15.7% to 72.4%. It suits high-volume, latency-sensitive work and subagent roles, while Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain better for complex coding.

title: Agent observability on the Claude Platform
summary: OpenTelemetry tracing for Claude Managed Agents, the Messages API, and SDKs is now in public beta. Teams add a destination in Claude Console, and each agent turn, model call, and tool use is exported as an OTel trace with latency, tokens, and IDs, following OTel GenAI semantic conventions for backends such as Grafana Cloud, Datadog, Langfuse, Splunk, or any OTLP endpoint. This lets teams review agent behavior before granting more access and track org-wide token usage.

title: Building effective agent automations
summary: Anthropic published a reference implementation of a scheduled 'daily brief' agent on Claude Managed Agents (beta) that reads Slack and GitHub PRs and posts to Slack. It is defined as config files applied with `ant apply`, keeps credentials in a vault outside the sandbox using read-only scoped tokens, and updates per-source bookmarks only after Slack confirms. Guardrails include a domain allowlist and a per-run spend cap, with a suggested starting cap of 3-5x normal run cost.

title: How the Claude Code team does code review
summary: Claude writes about 90% of Claude Code's code, and machines do most of the reading while humans handle decisions machines do poorly. Review runs continuously from before a PR exists, human approval scales by risk (none, one, or two reviewers), and past incidents feed an eval set that scores the reviewer. From June to September, merged PRs more than doubled and the revert share fell over 40%.

title: How Block orchestrates Claude Fable across thousands of pull requests
summary: Block's Bradley Axen describes using Claude Fable 5 as an orchestrator that handles high-level design and directs smaller models (Opus, Sonnet) for file edits and tests across migrations spanning thousands of PRs. The approach lowers cost without reported quality loss, and merges and production deploys still require security checks and two human approvals. Block is building an auto-selector to match model and effort level to each task.

title: Code Review is now generally available
summary: Claude Code's PR review feature is now generally available for Team and Enterprise organizations, and most reviews finish in 6-10 minutes, down from about 20 minutes in preview. Admins can set review depth per repo as Quick, Standard (the default), or Deep, and setup uses Claude Code settings plus a GitHub App, with reviews running automatically on new PRs. It targets review as the bottleneck now that coding agents speed up code creation.
